## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c6dcc41d165d4f258434a6d81ab10350522662c7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md, .github/workflows/fleet-patrols.yml, .github/workflows/fleet-write.yml + .github/CODEOWNERS

Read at 2026-11-16T02:57Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6905857127; lane request 6905843350 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Read: the diff `7be32d39..c6dcc41d` (one commit, 4 files, +36/−29), the PR body, the handoff comment 6905837616, card #33768 and its thread, and at this head `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs` (the `pr_dequeue` header, `DEQUEUE_CAUSES`, `DEQUEUE_FENCES`, `signedByLandingSeat`), `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs` (the grant pins), `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (`lowRiskArmVerdict`, `lowRiskRecordStageReasons`, the sweep's BREACH line), `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` (`codeownersMirrorVerdict`, the refusal remedies), `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (the `AGENTS.md` ceiling), `landing-operations.md`, `lanes/queue.md`, `platform-readings.md`, `contract-review.md`. Live reads: audit comment 6902190812, fleet-write run 43767458575 and its job log, the timeline of PR #34097, this head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

Each claim the new text makes, against what enforces it:

- **The dequeue stroke is measured — true.** Run 43767458575 (`fleet-write.yml`, `repository_dispatch`, concluded success) logged one action: the mint listed `permission-merge-queues: write`, `dequeuePullRequest` answered HTTP 200, the read-back listed 25 entries without #34097 and read the pull open and unmerged, audit comment 6902190812. The timeline of #34097 carries `removed_from_merge_queue` at 22:10:50 on 2026-11-15, re-queued and merged later the same day. Comment 6902190812 exists on #34097, is the relay's, and names cause `seat-asks` and the landing seat it read.
- **"Its landing seat" is the relay's fence for the cause that applies — true.** `DEQUEUE_CAUSE_JUDGES['seat-asks']` holds only when the pull body's signed trailer names a seat and a fleet comment signed by that same lane, seat number and account under the dispatching session sits on the pull. The other two causes (`conflict`, `own-failure`) are open to any dispatching seat but hold only on the relay's own readings of the entry, so they are not a route a seat can choose for a governed PR that should not be queued. `landing-operations.md` (the three causes) and `lanes/queue.md` (the queue seat acts for an offline landing seat under the first two; the third is the trailer's seat only) say the same. No contradiction.
- **The arm's two security conditions — true, and neither invented.** `lowRiskRecordStageReasons` keeps the arm at Tier H unless the review of record on the head carries exactly one bare `Security-touching: no` line and every card the PR names was read and neither carries the `security` label nor shows it removed in its timeline. "Ever labelled" is that label-or-removed read. The placement in the Tier S parenthetical beside `lowRiskArmVerdict` is right: that is where the arm's landing condition is stated, and the CODEOWNERS routing sentence lower down is about who is asked.
- **`fleet-write.yml` comment — true.** Two rows carry the merge-queue grant, each alone in its stroke (`validate.mjs` pins "the grant is this row's and the dequeue's alone" and an empty value on every other stroke). The cited `ops.mjs` header "The one row that takes a pull OUT of the merge queue" exists and says the same about the unmeasured half.
- **`fleet-patrols.yml` BREACH — true.** The sweep prints "no same-head at-tier PASS record, or a record stage at Tier H".
- **CODEOWNERS header — true.** `codeownersMirrorVerdict` wants no line for a Tier H row carrying the arm and reds if one is added; the header's title now agrees with its own section line and with the function. `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` is still named in the header, which the function requires.
- **The two compressions lose nothing.** "A PASS `## Contract review` record" is the same condition as "a record … and a PASS verdict". "The owning seat queues it" for "lands it through the queue": the queue is this repository's only landing route, the directive's first sentence still says Tier S lands "by the owning seat", and the duty to watch a queued PR to its landing lives in `landing-operations.md`, not in this clause.
- **Comment-only under `.github/` — confirmed.** Every changed line in the three files starts with `#`; no owner row, path row, workflow key, `with:` value or step moved.
- **Line budget — holds.** `AGENTS.md` is 1050 lines at the head against the ratchet's `['AGENTS.md', 1050]`; no touched line exceeds 120 bytes. The two self-tests the PR names were read, not run: nothing in `codeownersMirrorVerdict` reads comment text beyond the constant's name, and no gate pins a phrase this diff changed outside the queue guard's own remedy text (S2).

### ② Semver level

None. Nothing publishes; the PR carries `skip-changeset` and declares `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, both correct for rules text and comments.

CI at this head, 51 check-runs: 28 success, 18 skipped, 5 still in progress (Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Test UI 1/16), none failed. Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green. ⛔ This PASS is on the text; the seat waits for the five running checks before treating the head as green.

CI completed before posting: 53 check-runs on this head, 35 success, 18 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier H: the diff touches `AGENTS.md` and two workflows, and `.github/CODEOWNERS` is an enforcement-chain row. It stays draft and lands only on an approval by a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account. This record is the contract review, not that approval.
- File surface held as claimed: `AGENTS.md` changes sit inside Prime Directive 14 only; CODEOWNERS header comments only; workflow comment lines only.
- `Part of #33768` is right: N1, E1, D2, D4 and N2 stay open on the card.
- No security finding at the rule layer.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — `AGENTS.md` PD14, the dequeue sentence: the landing seat is given the relay stroke and nothing for the case where the stroke does not land. Before this PR every seat was told to ask the maintainer at once; now only "any other seat" is. The relay refuses or fails a dequeue on several readings (`DEQUEUE_FENCES`, exit 5; a FAILED read-back), and `lanes/queue.md` tells only the queue seat to report a FAILED stroke to the maintainer. On the one sentence that is the backstop for a governed PR sitting in the queue, the landing seat should not have to guess. A wording that costs no line: "for a queued one its landing seat sends the relay's `pr_dequeue` (measured live, comment 6902190812); any other seat, or a stroke that does not land, asks the maintainer at once to remove it by hand". That also puts "at once" back on the asking, where the old sentence had it (it now reads as the pace of the maintainer's removal).

S2 (should-fix) — two followers of this change have no filed carrier. After this lands, the queue guard's refusal remedies (`check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, both refusal texts and two comments) still tell every seat that no seat act is measured to dequeue; that is the text a seat actually sees at the moment PD14's sentence applies, and it will disagree with PD14. And `platform-readings.md`, the home of measured platform readings, has no row for the dequeue stroke, so PD14 leans on a comment id alone. The PR body names "the seat" as carrier for both and points the second at the card's N1/E1 step, which records two other measurements. Add both as checklist items on #33768 (or a card of their own for the guard text, which is a Tier H enforcement-chain edit) before this lands. No change to this diff is asked.

N1 (nit) — "measured live, comment 6902190812": the comment is the relay's audit comment posted before the mutation; it states the cause and says the outcome is on the run's row. The measurement itself is in run 43767458575 and in the pull's `removed_from_merge_queue` timeline event. The citation is findable and true; the reading row of S2 is the durable anchor.

N2 (nit) — `fleet-write.yml`: "… is NOT MEASURED until the first live stroke …; nor is whether `dequeuePullRequest` needs this grant at all" reads as if a first live dequeue stroke would settle it. That stroke has happened and settled only that a token with the grant works. "is NOT MEASURED either: the one live stroke carried the grant" would say what is known.

N3 (nit) — PD14 arm parenthetical: "no named card ever labelled `security`" reads as satisfied by a PR that names no card, while the reader refuses a PR with no derivable card or an unread one; and the PR's own `security` label, which the arm also refuses, is not named. `lowRiskArmVerdict` is cited as the one full statement, so nothing is wrong; noted so nobody reads the parenthetical as the whole list.

N4 (nit) — "a PASS `## Contract review` record for its current head": "its" follows "the PR thread or its card" and now leans on the reader to bind it to the PR. The old "the PR's current head" was exact.

N5 (nit) — operability for a non-landing seat when the maintainer is away: the text offers only the maintainer, as before this PR. The landing seat can now remove the PR itself, so telling it is the faster route; one clause in `landing-operations.md` would do, outside this diff.

Duplication check: PD14 states who sends the dequeue in the governed case and points at no second copy of the three causes; `landing-operations.md` and `lanes/queue.md` keep those. The `Security-touching:` line's values stay in the record template; `contract-review.md` only points there. No rule is restated in two places by this diff.

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S1 in this diff, S2 on the card).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

### ① Derived judgments

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1 — closed.** PD14 now reads "a queued one's landing seat sends the relay's `pr_dequeue` (measured live, comment 6902190812); any other seat, or a stroke that does not land, asks the maintainer at once — then confirm from the remote that it is in neither the queue nor `origin/main`". The landing seat has its backstop, and "at once" is on the asking again. It is operable: `pr_dequeue` carries no draft fence (`DEQUEUE_FENCES`: open, head, release, queue, queued, and the cause), so the paragraph's first act (back to draft) does not block its second; a refused stroke (exit 5) and a FAILED read-back are both "a stroke that does not land". It agrees with the skill: `landing-operations.md` keeps the three causes and gives cause (c) to the seat the PR body's signed trailer names; `lanes/queue.md` says a FAILED stroke is not resent and goes to the maintainer. The dropped "to remove it by hand" is judged acceptable: the paragraph is about a queued governed PR, and the clause that follows states the end state the maintainer is asked for. See N1 for the wording.
- **S2 — closed, in changed form.** Carry-over note 6905853116 on #33768 names both followers (the queue guard's refusal hints in `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`; a `platform-readings.md` row for the live dequeue, run 43767458575) and sequences them after this PR. That is the carrier this card has used for its two earlier carry-over items, both of which were picked up from the thread. They are notes in the thread, not boxes in the card body; see N2.
- **N1 (citation is the audit comment, not the measurement) — open, not taken, accepted.** The citation is true and findable; the durable anchor is the S2 reading row.
- **N2 (`fleet-write.yml` "nor is whether") — closed.** The note now reads "Whether `dequeuePullRequest` needs this grant at all, or what a token without it answers, is NOT MEASURED either: the one live stroke carried the grant", which is exactly what run 43767458575 established. The cited `ops.mjs` header still exists under that title.
- **N3 (arm parenthetical is not the whole list) — open, not taken, accepted.** `lowRiskArmVerdict` stays cited as the full statement.
- **N4 ("its current head") — closed.** "for the PR's current head", no line added.
- **N5 (a non-landing seat's faster route is the landing seat) — open, outside this diff, no carrier.** Continued as N3 below.

The delta itself:

- **The merge brought nothing into the four paths.** `git diff 2198eb03a af9ef8f08` over `AGENTS.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `fleet-write.yml`, `fleet-patrols.yml` is empty: main changed none of them between `7be32d39` and `b8456ebd`.
- **No rule PD14 cites moved under it.** The seven commits main brought (#34205, #34139, #34169, #34222, #34043, #34202, #34019) touch nothing under `scripts/pm/**` or `.github/**`. #34222 edits `lanes/queue.md`, `project-forms.md` and `triage-duties.md`: the queue lane's jump lines are folded into a pointer and triage, when it covers the queue charter, is told not to ask the maintainer for what the relay can do. The dequeue line is untouched, and the new clause agrees with PD14, which sends to the maintainer only what the relay did not or cannot do for that seat. #34202 (the MCP confirmation-gated action) is product code and names no rule here.
- **Comment-only under `.github/` — confirmed for the whole PR.** Against main `b8456ebd`, every changed line in the three files starts with `#`; zero non-comment lines.
- **Line budget — holds.** `AGENTS.md` is 1050 lines at this head against the ratchet's `['AGENTS.md', 1050]`; the touched PD14 lines are 118 to 120 bytes.

### ② Semver level

None. Nothing publishes; `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` stay correct for rules text and comments.

The cancelled run is the first PR-body guards run, superseded by a later run of the same check that is green (the body was patched after the push). Governed Surface Queue Guard and Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests are green. ⛔ This PASS is on the text; the seat waits for the eight running checks before treating the head as green.

CI completed before posting: 52 check-runs on this head, 34 success, 17 skipped, 1 cancelled (the superseded first PR-body guards run; its re-run is green), none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier H, unchanged: `AGENTS.md`, two workflows, and `.github/CODEOWNERS` as an enforcement-chain row. The PR is draft and lands only on an approval by a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account. This record is the contract review, not that approval.
- File surface held: round 1 touched PD14 only in `AGENTS.md` and comment lines only in `fleet-write.yml`; `CODEOWNERS` and `fleet-patrols.yml` are byte-identical to `c6dcc41d`.
- `Part of #33768` stays right: N1, E1, D2, D4, N2 and the two followers of 6905853116 remain on the card.
- No security finding at the rule layer.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit, new; follows prior S1) — the backstop clause makes "a stroke that does not land" the subject of "asks the maintainer", and no longer says what is asked. A reader gets it from the paragraph and from the confirm clause, so nothing is wrong; if PD14 ever frees about 25 bytes, "any other seat, or the landing seat whose stroke does not land, asks the maintainer at once to remove it" is the exact form. Not worth a ceiling raise.

N2 (nit; continues prior S2) — the two followers live in thread note 6905853116, while the card body's checklist has no box for them, and the PR body still names two other carriers in its Acceptance notes ("a `domain:skills` tooling card", "the card's N1/E1 recording step") beside the Review round 1 line that names the note. Add two boxes to the card body when this lands and align the Acceptance notes. The note should also say that the guard's refusal text is a Tier H enforcement-chain edit, so whoever takes it opens it as one.

N3 (nit; continues prior N5) — a non-landing seat that finds a governed PR queued is sent to the maintainer only; telling the PR's landing seat is the faster route now that it can dequeue. One clause in `landing-operations.md`, outside this diff; it has no carrier and could ride the same card note.

Prior N1 and N3 stand as accepted nits with no further ask.

Duplication check: the delta restates no rule. PD14 still names who sends the dequeue in the governed case and leaves the three causes to `landing-operations.md` and `lanes/queue.md`.
